clinical_notes: 77 y/o female with chronic low back pain radiating down the left leg. Completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy including core strengthening and lumbar stabilization, plus a course of NSAIDs, without meaningful improvement. Exam reveals positive straight-leg raise at 30° on the left, 4/5 weakness of the second-toe extensor, diminished Achilles reflex, and S1 dermatomal sensory loss. Ordered by neurosurgery for pre-operative planning of an L4-L5 decompression.
ground_truth_reasoning: C.1 met: 10 weeks documented PT + NSAIDs with no improvement.
C.2 met: motor deficit and reflex change on exam.
C.3 met: radicular pattern correlates with L4-L5 distribution.
C.4 met: ordered for surgical planning.
All coverage criteria satisfied → APPROVED.
policy_excerpt:
LCD L34522 — Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Lumbar Spine
§C.1: Documented failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy, including physical therapy, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications, or activity modification, without clinically significant improvement.
§C.2: Persistent neurological symptoms that correlate with imaging: motor deficit, dermatomal sensory loss, reflex changes, or bowel/bladder dysfunction suggestive of cauda equina syndrome.
§C.3: The clinical presentation must plausibly correlate with lumbar pathology; pain alone without neurological or functional findings is insufficient.
§C.4: The imaging is ordered to plan a specific surgical or interventional procedure, or to rule out a surgical lesion when conservative measures have failed.
§L.1: Repeat lumbar MRI within 12 months of a prior study requires documentation of a new neurologic deficit, significant clinical change, or post-operative evaluation. Routine surveillance MRI is not covered.
§L.2: Routine screening MRI for nonspecific low back pain without neurological findings is not a covered indication.
§L.3: MRI performed solely for administrative purposes (employment physicals, insurance underwriting, legal proceedings) is not covered.

clinical_notes: 72 y/o female with 1 weeks of low back pain. Has tried over-the-counter ibuprofen and a single visit to physical therapy. No formal PT course completed. Exam is nonfocal: full strength, intact reflexes, negative straight-leg raise. Patient requests MRI to see 'what's causing the pain.'
ground_truth_reasoning: C.1 unmet: only 1 weeks of informal conservative therapy, no completed PT course.
C.2 unmet: exam is nonfocal, no neurological deficit.
Criteria not satisfied → DENIED (medical necessity).

clinical_notes: 77 y/o female with 5-day history of severe low back pain and new urinary hesitancy. Initial submission from primary care noted only 'low back pain, requests MRI.' Payer denied for missing clinical information. On resubmission with full exam documentation — reduced perianal sensation, post-void residual 300 mL, reduced anal tone — the appeal was granted citing concern for cauda equina syndrome.
ground_truth_reasoning: Initial denial: MISSING_INFO (inadequate exam documentation).
On appeal: full documentation shows perianal sensory loss, urinary retention, reduced anal tone.
C.2 clearly met on appeal: red-flag cauda equina signs.
C.3 met: findings localize to sacral roots.
Appeal panel reversed the denial → OVERTURNED ON APPEAL.

clinical_notes: 62 y/o male with 4-week history of low back pain now reporting rapidly progressive right-sided weakness. Had been attempting home exercise but did not complete formal PT because symptoms escalated. Exam: 2/5 extensor hallucis longus weakness, foot slap gait, hyperreflexia at the knee, clonus absent. Progressive deficit documented on two visits separated by 4 days. Ordered for urgent surgical consultation.
ground_truth_reasoning: C.1 technically unmet: formal 6-week conservative trial not completed.
Progressive motor deficit provides clinical override of C.1 per standard medical necessity.
C.2 strongly met: rapidly worsening motor findings.
C.3 met: level localizes clinically.
C.4 met: ordered for urgent surgical decision.
Progressive deficit overrides conservative trial → APPROVED.

clinical_notes: 44 y/o female presenting with sudden severe low back pain 48 hours ago and new saddle-distribution numbness. No urinary retention yet. No bowel incontinence. Exam: reduced perianal sensation, preserved anal tone, bilateral right L5-S1 sensory changes. PT not attempted given emergent presentation. Ordered to rule out cauda equina syndrome.
ground_truth_reasoning: C.1 not required: emergent indication bypasses conservative trial.
C.2 met: perianal sensory deficit raises cauda equina concern.
C.3 met: findings correlate with lumbosacral distribution.
C.4 met: rule-out surgical emergency.
Emergent indication → APPROVED.
